title: The Witness of Greywater Bay
premise: Sebastian Nakamura, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has made them the quiet keeper of Greywater Bay's buried truths, receives two letters on the same morning: one confessing to the drowning of pearl diver Elena Vasquez five years ago, and one promising a second death unless Sebastian burns every file they've ever kept. As Sebastian reopens the case everyone swore was closed, they discover the letters come from two different hands—one from a dying man seeking absolution, one from his accomplice protecting a fortune in laundered inheritance. With the help of the Vasquez family, who adopt Sebastian into their orbit of grief and grit, Sebastian must choose between the law that failed Elena and a justice of their own making, ending with the accomplice exposed at the bay's edge and Sebastian finally surrendering their files—not to the police, but to the family who deserved them.
about_author: Marguerite Lockridge is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipwreck claims along the Pacific coast before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about small towns where the water keeps better secrets than the people do.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Morning
chapters.summary: Sebastian Nakamura's POV. On the fifth anniversary of Elena Vasquez's drowning, Sebastian receives two unsigned letters: a confession and a threat. The emotional beat is dread disguised as routine—Sebastian's ordered world cracks open as memory floods back with photographic precision.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Flashbacks interweave with the present as Sebastian reviews their private files on Greywater Bay's residents, realizing the confession's details match something they saw but never reported. The beat is guilt: staying invisible was a choice, and it had a cost.

chapters.title: The Vasquez Table
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, first meeting with Marisol Vasquez, Elena's sister, at the family's struggling oyster bar. Marisol recognizes Sebastian from the inquest. The beat is tentative connection—two people circling the same wound, neither ready to name it.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returned
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A second letter arrives with a physical clue: Elena's missing dive watch. Forensics point to Harlan Creed, the town's dying patriarch, but the handwriting doesn't match his known correspondence. The beat is sharpening suspicion—someone else is steering this.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Parlor
chapters.summary: Sebastian confronts Harlan Creed, who neither confirms nor denies, but slips one detail only a participant would know. His heir, Daniel Creed, watches with cold amusement. The beat is vertigo—Sebastian realizes the confession may be genuine while the threat comes from another hand entirely.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The Vasquez household absorbs Sebastian—Sunday dinners, Elena's old room, stories the official record never held. The beat is warmth and terror intertwined: for the first time, Sebastian has something to lose.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The threats escalate: Sebastian's office is ransacked, half their archive stolen, and a third letter sets a deadline—the remaining files or Marisol. The beat is cornered fury; invisibility is no longer protection but bait.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Ledger
chapters.summary: Sebastian reconstructs the stolen files from memory, uncovering a laundering scheme funneling Elena's insurance payout through Creed holdings into Daniel's accounts. The beat is cold clarity—the motive was never silencing a killer; it was securing an inheritance built on her death.

chapters.title: Greywater Bay at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, climax. Lured to the bay under false pretenses, Sebastian faces Daniel, who confesses freely—he believes the water absolves everything. Harlan arrives to stop his son; Marisol arrives to finish what the law wouldn't. The beat is reckoning, violent and intimate, at the exact spot where Elena died.

chapters.title: Everything I Kept
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, resolution. Weeks later, Sebastian hands the entire archive to the Vasquez family—not the police—and lets the town's secrets settle where they belong. Harlan dies quietly; Daniel awaits trial on evidence that will hold. The beat is release: justice outside the law, and a home inside it.
